s.g: The condition of being movable; ability or capacity to be moved.
The ability to move (oneself).
Capable of being moved, lifted, carried, drawn, turned, or conveyed, or in any way made to change place or posture; not fixed or stationary.
Changing from one time to another.
s.x: Easter is a movable holiday.

s.g: Something which is movable; an article of wares or goods; a commodity; a piece of property not fixed, or not a part of real estate; generally, in the plural, goods; wares; furniture.
Such that it can be moved.
Removal (the transfer of one's home or business)
(law) The party who moves for the judge to rule in favor of a motion.
(intransitive) To change place or posture; to go, in any manner, from one place or position to another.
s.x: A ship moves rapidly.

s.g: (intransitive) To act; to take action; to begin to act
s.x: to move in a matter

s.g: (intransitive) To change residence, for example from one house, town, or state, to another; to go and live at another place; similarly to change the location of another establishment such as a business. See also move out and move in.
s.x: I decided to move to the country for a more peaceful life.

s.g: (transitive) To transport (an item) as part of changing residences.
s.x: Before my lease ended, I gave away my old sofa because I didn't want to move it.

s.g: (transitive, ergative) To cause to change place or posture in any manner; to set in motion; to carry, convey, draw, or push from one place to another
s.x: The waves moved the boat up and down.

s.g: The act of moving; a movement.
s.x: A slight move of the tiller, and the boat will go off course.

s.g: An act for the attainment of an object; a step in the execution of a plan or purpose.
s.x: He made another move towards becoming a naturalized citizen.

s.g: A formalized or practiced action used in athletics, dance, physical exercise, self-defense, hand-to-hand combat, etc.
s.x: She always gets spontaneous applause for that one move.

s.g: The event of changing one's residence.
s.x: The move into my fiancé's house took two long days.

s.g: A change in strategy.
s.x: I am worried about our boss's move.

s.g: Emotionally affected; touched.
s.x: What happened to that girl in the film was so awful – I was extremely moved.

s.g: (obsolete) Convinced.

moved.f: simple past and past participle of move

s.g: Physical motion between points in space.
s.x: I saw a movement in that grass on the hill.

s.g: (engineering) A system or mechanism for transmitting motion of a definite character, or for transforming motion, such as the wheelwork of a watch.
The impression of motion in an artwork, painting, novel etc.
A trend in various fields or social categories, a group of people with a common ideology who try together to achieve certain general goals.
s.x: social movement

s.g: (music) A large division of a larger composition.
s.x: Beethoven's movements

movement.f: Ellipsis of bowel movement (“an act of emptying the bowels”).

s.g: Someone who or something that moves.
A dancer.
A person employed to help people move their possessions from one residence to another.
s.x: I'm getting too old to expect my friends to schlep all my stuff for beer and pizza. I'm hiring movers this time.

s.g: Someone who proposes a motion at a meeting.
A product that sells well.
A good ability to dance.
s.x: Check out the guy on the dancefloor, he's got seriously good moves.

moves.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of move

s.g: (video games) The set of moves that a character can perform.

moveth.f: (archaic) third-person singular simple present indicative of move

s.g: (chiefly Canada, US, Australia, New Zealand) A recorded sequence of images displayed on a screen at a rate sufficiently fast to create the appearance of motion; a film; a video.

A professionally made motion picture of a substantive narrative work, typically around 1 to 3 hours long, typically intended for cinema, art, entertainment, and a widespread audience; a feature film, theatrical film.
s.x: My favorite actor is starring in the new movie.

s.g: (usually in the plural, chiefly Canada, US, Australia, New Zealand) A cinema; a movie theatre.
s.x: Let's go to the movies.

s.g: (informal, figuratively) Any event, especially one that is unpleasant or tiresome.
s.x: Don't worry; this isn't the first time I've been through this movie.

s.g: (slang, figuratively) An extremely fun and exciting experience.
s.x: Every night with you is a movie!

s.g: (chiefly Canada, US) Person who regularly frequents movie theaters.
Attending movies, especially habitually or regularly.
The act of attending movies.
The industry of films and filmmaking.
The fictitious world where films are set.
A person who makes movies as a profession; a cinematographer.
The production of movies
s.x: Moviemaking is a very different art from stage production.

s.g: (by extension, chiefly Canada, US, Australia) The cinema
s.x: We are going to the movies for our anniversary.

s.g: (not comparable) That moves or move.
s.x: moving pictures

s.g: Causing or evoking deep emotions.

moving.f: present participle and gerund of move

s.g: (uncountable) The relocation of goods when transferring one's household, business, etc., to another location
(countable) A causing of a movement
s.x: The rats' movings are willed movements.

s.g: In a moving manner.
(film, historical) An early machine allowing a film editor to view the film while editing it.
